claims.statement: The agent derives resumed model history from its JSONL log, skips crash-truncated lines, and records compaction without deleting older messages or splitting call-result pairs.

Entirely read-only permitted tool batches run concurrently and preserve completed outcomes and usage when cancelled, marking only unfinished calls interrupted; other batches execute in order and distinguish interrupted calls from calls not run.
RPC plan gating rejects file mutations and mutating MCP calls; outside-sandbox bash asks every time while sandboxing is on, regardless of the normal approval mode.
Sandboxing defaults on, is configured by CLI then environment and user sandbox.json, and refuses commands if the machine cannot sandbox; file tools follow the same access view.
File edits and overwrites are refused after an observed file changes until reread, using recorded size, modification time and hash.
In-process task subagents have restricted tools, cannot recursively delegate or use desktop tools, share approval and cancellation, and run at most four at a time.
Sandbox tests cover hidden secrets through symlinks and parent traversal and prevent broad working directories from making the whole home writable.
Provider settings support Responses and chat-completions endpoints and are reread for each request.
Usage accounting separates cached input and cost classification; budgets count uncached input, output and estimates of missing usage, while mixed priced/unknown requests yield partly known cost.
Provider configuration supports per-million-token prices and thinking-level mappings, while built-in Responses web search is limited to plan/OpenAI routes and can be disabled by environment.
Unpriced providers require explicit free=true for local/no-extra-cost classification regardless of address; configured or listed model pricing takes precedence over that flag.

Missing either input or output token usage increments unreported counts and makes priced requests unknown-cost; logs, aggregate details and subagent totals preserve uncertainty and separate budget-only estimates.

Cutoff attempts, including missing-usage estimates, and failed attempts with error usage or a retained stream-usage snapshot are charged immediately into a session-owned ledger; settlement logs them separately from successful replies before fallback, after tool batches and on stop, so dropping retry work does not discard recorded spend.

Shared budget admission atomically reserves estimated request tokens plus 2000 tokens of reply room across main, side, compaction and web-search requests; every retry and post-native-compaction summary obtains fresh admission, with spent-plus-held limits that admitted requests can overshoot.
Fallback records and announces the model change then restarts the run-loop request path rather than resending an already prepared request for the old model.
Completed side-question usage is attributed to its originating session log even after switching sessions, and RPC shutdown waits at most ten seconds for outstanding side tasks before settling usage.
MCP servers start concurrently with a default ten-second startup timeout; after two seconds the agent reports still-pending servers and their timeout allowance.

File reads deliver nested rules once while present in history, while edits encountering unseen rules stop before changing anything and return those rules for reconsideration; hidden/dependency folders are skipped, rules are capped at 8 KB, and delivery state is rebuilt after history changes.
Large-file reads retain a bounded line selection and whole-file hash, while grep incrementally processes output with bounded preview and spill behavior rather than collecting all matches in memory.
Foreground shell execution drains stdout and stderr independently and cleans up its process group on cancellation, timeout, dropped futures, and command completion.
Provider refusal text is bounded to 64 KiB within the response timeout, and completed SSE events are checked against the event-size limit before delivery.
Explore-only sandbox views explicitly mount the project and shared Git directory read-only even under writable ancestors; this shell-level guarantee requires sandboxing.
Isolated subagent tree capture excludes Python bytecode and common Python tool caches, preventing cache changes from blocking real edits during merge-back.
Web searches settle token spend before releasing their budget holds, and parent tool-result aggregation adds usage without charging that spend twice.
Stop interrupts desktop-tool discovery and MCP startup; an incomplete MCP start is retried on a subsequent prompt.

MCP schemas exceeding a configurable 12000-byte threshold are replaced by tool search and indirect calls, with up to eight search matches; indirect calls resolve before read-only, approval and plan checks.
Overlong read lines report truncation and continuation guidance; file-name search streams paths while retaining only a bounded alphabetically first set and the total count.

Side questions, native compaction and summary requests, and web searches settle failed or cut-off attempts separately from a successful reply; side usage queues and the session ledger retain those attempts independently of the request future.

Nested rules delivered within a tool batch block subsequent changes under the same folder until the next batch, including after direct rules-file reads and for move destinations; unrelated folders remain writable.

Indirect MCP arguments normalize objects or JSON-object strings, treating absent/null/blank values as empty objects and rejecting other shapes; tool names resolve by full exposed name or unambiguous bare or server-qualified name.
run_code exposes concrete permitted read-only MCP tools but excludes the generic mcp_call dispatcher from its callable set.

Chat-completions usage reports merge recursively: later non-null fields replace earlier totals, omitted fields remain, and error-local usage overlays accumulated usage before normalization; measured zero remains zero and wholly absent failed-reply usage remains absent.

Broken chat-completions streams preserve previously reported usage in Dropped errors, which the agent charges before retry admission; a dropped stream without reported usage does not add a failed-attempt charge.

Stopping an in-flight chat request charges its latest recognized normalized usage once through Tries::stopped, also invoked on drop; compaction and model-change summary sends invoke it before ledger settlement, normal completion clears the snapshot to avoid duplicate charges, and a stop without recognized counts adds no guard charge.

Chat token counts normalize independently, preserving output-only or input-only measurements without inventing the missing count; the focused partial-count test verifies that missing input is estimated for budget accounting while remaining unreported.

Harlo agent imports enabled skills from Claude Code's installed user/project plugins alongside normal skill folders, applies settings-based disablement and project applicability, deduplicates matching plugin skills against ordinary skills, and exposes skills through bounded instruction listings and explicit `/skill:` prompt expansion.

The Claude harness converts completion events for detached Claude-managed shells and subagents into retained custom transcript notices, formatting a command-only stopped-shell summary with its command and stopped status. This adapter path is distinct from Harlo's in-process task subagents and desktop helper sessions.

The native Messages adapter reconstructs provider request turns from shared history, carries thinking signatures only when provider and model match, and replaces images with an explicit note when the model does not support them.

The Gemini adapter translates shared history into Gemini contents and restores thought signatures and call IDs only for their originating provider/model; foreign function calls receive Google's no-signature placeholder.

Harlo's own tool list is gated by caller identity and project state: wiki writers receive authoring tools, wiki-enabled ordinary project sessions receive reading tools only when a wiki exists, and plan tools require the project's plan setting.
A helper handed steps in a shared plan cannot mutate those steps through plan_set, plan_start, or plan_done until the run ends.
